title: Dewan Kaura Mal Appeals to the Singhs

blocks.text: As Abdali’s advance unsettles Lahore and Sirhind, local calculations change quickly. The page shows how men who once maneuvered within Mughal politics begin seeking stronger partners, because the Afghan threat makes older arrangements look fragile and incomplete.

The key development is that Dewan Kaura Mal invites the Singhs into alliance instead of treating them as expendable auxiliaries. He offers assurance, support, and recognition in exchange for help against Abdali, giving the Khalsa a role defined by negotiation rather than mere persecution.

This marks a major shift in the story’s political logic. The Singhs are acknowledged as a power whose friendship matters, and Kaura Mal emerges as the courtly figure most willing to bind his fortunes to theirs.
